Large floods do not occur at random

Demystifying surprise floods across eight thousand years in the Upper Tennessee Basin


C l i n c h · F re n c h B ro a d · O co e e




Spencer Livingston, PhD Student, Department of Geography and Environment (spencer.livingston@ua.edu)

Lisa Davis, Professor, Department of Geography and Environment (lisa.davis@ua.edu)
 Study sites and records
                          The catalog
 MAP

                          Ocoee                           188 floods          0–8,000 BP


 Upper Tennessee Basin
                          French Broad                    170 floods          0–8,000 BP



                          Clinch                          97 floods           0–8,000 BP




                          455 river-age entries pooled, including 81 flagged extremes.
                          All selected events are large floods. Median ages are fixed.
                          Four repeated Ocoee ages follow the draft’s merge convention.
 THE RECORD


Upper Tennessee flood record, 0–8,000 BP




250-year bins. Red points identify the 81 flagged extremes within the 455-entry catalog. Horizontal axis: age in years BP.
 THE QUESTION


What do paleofloods reveal about extreme flood behavior?

     Paleofloods reveal departures from constant-rate timing that short gage records cannot resolve.
 METHODS


Interevent spacing and epoch stacking

Interevent spacing                                                                                      Epoch stacking

η = standard deviation / mean gap                                                                       Clustering timescale around each flood

Interevent spacing tests whether the sequence                                                           Center the record on every large flood and count
departs from random, but it does not show the                                                           neighboring floods at each lag.
temporal footprint around individual floods.
                                                                                                        The first positive lag where the curve returns inside
                                                                                                        the 95% null envelope defines the clustering
                                                                                                        timescale.


Each test uses the same event count and fixed analysis window. The null assumes uniform event timing.

1,999 simulations. Full timeline: 0–8,000 BP. Late Holocene: 0–4,000 BP. Mid Holocene: 4,000–8,000 BP. Lag is neighbor age minus reference age.
 POOLED BASIN


Pooled results across the full timeline and both eras


 Window                                                  n                    Gap variability η                             Clustering p   Stack p

 0–8,000 BP                                              455                  1.29                                          <0.001         <0.001

 0–4,000 BP                                              307                  1.61                                          <0.001         <0.001

 4,000–8,000 BP                                          148                  0.87                                          0.963          0.572



Pooling establishes the timing pattern of the combined catalog. Synchrony between rivers requires a separate test.




Distinct equal-age observations remain in the pool. Removing zero gaps reproduces draft η values of 1.24, 1.53, and 0.86.
 RIVER INTEREVENT SPACING


Extreme flood timing departs from a constant-rate process




Ocoee clusters in every window. French Broad at 4–8 ka and Clinch at 0–4 ka do not reject uniform spacing.

Open markers: p ≥ 0.05. η = 1: exponential-process reference. Seven river results remain significant after BH adjustment across 12 CV tests.
 RIVER EPOCH STACKS


Return to the null envelope defines the clustering timescale

 Ocoee p < 0.001                                                      French Broad p < 0.001                                               Clinch p = 0.111
 Above envelope through +325 yr                                       First return at +250 yr                                              No sustained central exceedance




French Broad first returns inside the envelope at +250 years. Ocoee remains above it through +325 years. Clinch has no
sustained central exceedance to time.
0–4,000 BP. Blue: observed. Gray: pointwise 95% null envelope. Positive lag provides the reporting convention; the stacks are symmetric.
 COLD PERIODS


Cold periods provide a midlatitude climate context

van Dijk et al. (2024) link prolonged Northern Hemisphere cooling
to clustered volcanic forcing and ocean–sea-ice feedbacks.




2,200 years inside cold windows                                                                                       27.5% of the 8,000-year interval

Cold-period membership tests an association with flood timing. It does not establish a local volcanic mechanism.

Supplied 200-year windows match Table 1 using the supplied BP conversion. Cold-time coverage: 30% at 0–4 ka and 25% at 4–8 ka.
 COLD-PERIOD ASSOCIATION


Observed flood rates align with cold periods in this basin

 Catalog                                                     0–8,000 BP                                      0–4,000 BP                  4,000–8,000 BP

 Basin pooled                                                1.68×                                           1.74×                       1.35×

 Ocoee                                                       2.27×                                           2.45×                       1.76×

 French Broad                                                1.55×                                           1.77×                       0.56×

 Clinch                                                      1.02×                                           0.63×                       1.66×

Rate ratio = (inside floods / cold years) ÷ (outside floods / other years)

The full timeline and both eras are shown side by side. Uneven preservation limits causal interpretation of differences
among intervals.
Observed rate ratios describe the selected catalog. They are neither clustering statistics nor modern annual exceedance probabilities.
 COLD-PERIOD TIMING


Cold versus non-cold timing within one era




This 0–4 ka visual is an example from the denser preserved interval. The previous slide carries the full-timeline and era comparisons.
 Large floods show statistically significant temporal clustering


Statistical evidence of temporal clustering
Across the full timeline and both eras, seven of nine river-window tests reject the constant-
rate null.

Cold periods provide a partial explanation
The observed flood rate is higher during cold periods overall, but the association varies by
river and era. Cold periods may help concentrate large floods without explaining the full
timing pattern.

 HAZARD


One discharge, three different hazards

                                                                                                                                                     80,000 cfs


                                                                                                                                                     28-yr
                                                                                                                                                     in the gage record



                                                                                                                                                     12-yr
                                                                                                                                                     during burst intervals



                                                                                                                                                     49-yr
                                                                                                                                                     during quiet intervals

                                                                                                                                                     R = 4.17×



The gage curve is not too high or too low, it is a blended average that overstates hazard in quiet intervals and understates it in bursts.

Split conserves the long-term mean: bursts occupy ≈23% of the record, quiet intervals ≈77%, and their time-weighted average returns the LP3 value.
 BACKUP


Preservation sensitivity in the recent record

 Pooled, 0–8,000 BP                                                                       All cold windows                                          Youngest window removed

 Inside-cold events                                                                       177                                                       90

 Inside-cold exposure                                                                     2,200 years                                               2,000 years

 Inside / outside rate                                                                    1.68×                                                     0.94×

87 of 177 inside-cold entries fall at 310–110 BP.
Removing that window also removes its 200 years of exposure.

A shift test that preserves existing clusters gives p = 0.086 for the full-record rate association.

9,999 random circular shifts within each era. The 100-year neighbor-density contrast gives p = 0.170. These are sensitivity tests with circular-boundary assumptions.
